title: Why School Sucks (Game Theory Explains It)
alt_titles: School Isn't Broken. It's Doing Exactly What We Reward.
The Real Reason School Feels Pointless (Game Theory)
He Fixed School. Then They Fired Him.
description:
Why does school so often reward memorizing, looking good and easy grades instead of real thinking? Game theory has an uncomfortable answer: school may not be broken at all. It may be working exactly as its players' incentives reward it to.

We follow a Yale English major who built a school program in Shenzhen that sent students to Yale, Wharton and Cornell, and then got fired, and use game theory (players, incentives, power) to see why great results were not enough.

CHAPTERS
0:00 Cold open: the 3 jobs of school
0:45 The experiment: a Yale grad in Shenzhen
1:28 The school everyone says they want
2:23 Meet the players
3:56 Who has the power?
5:03 Why some schools escape
6:14 The real lesson
7:06 The ending: change the game

IDEAS IN THIS VIDEO
- Players, incentives and power: parents, teachers, administrators, government, colleges, students
- Why "bold reform" turns into "don't cause trouble"
- Cohesion, openness and energy: three forces that decide whether schools improve or decline
- How to change the payoffs, not just the slogans

Topic inspired by Professor Jiang Xueqin's Predictive History lecture series. This video is an original script, original animation and original narration. The Shenzhen story is told as that lecture presents it; details are his account and are not independently verified.

What mattered most in your school: learning, or looking successful? Tell me in the comments.
